require 'forwardable'

require_relative 'dirtyable'

module Zip
  class CentralDirectory # :nodoc:
    extend Forwardable
    include Dirtyable

    END_OF_CD_SIG          = 0x06054b50
    ZIP64_END_OF_CD_SIG    = 0x06064b50
    ZIP64_EOCD_LOCATOR_SIG = 0x07064b50

    STATIC_EOCD_SIZE       = 22
    ZIP64_STATIC_EOCD_SIZE = 56
    ZIP64_EOCD_LOC_SIZE    = 20
    MAX_FILE_COMMENT_SIZE  = (1 << 16) - 1
    MAX_END_OF_CD_SIZE     =
      MAX_FILE_COMMENT_SIZE + STATIC_EOCD_SIZE + ZIP64_EOCD_LOC_SIZE

    attr_accessor :comment

    def_delegators :@entry_set,
                   :<<, :delete, :each, :entries, :find_entry, :glob,
                   :include?, :size

    mark_dirty :<<, :comment=, :delete

    def initialize(entries = EntrySet.new, comment = '') # :nodoc:
      super(dirty_on_create: false)
      @entry_set = entries.kind_of?(EntrySet) ? entries : EntrySet.new(entries)
      @comment   = comment
    end

    def read_from_stream(io)
      read_eocds(io)
      read_central_directory_entries(io)
    end

    def write_to_stream(io, suppress_extra_fields: false) # :nodoc:
      cdir_offset = io.tell
      @entry_set.each do |entry|
        entry.write_c_dir_entry(io, suppress_extra_fields: suppress_extra_fields)
      end
      eocd_offset = io.tell
      cdir_size = eocd_offset - cdir_offset
      if Zip.write_zip64_support &&
         (cdir_offset > 0xFFFFFFFF || cdir_size > 0xFFFFFFFF || @entry_set.size > 0xFFFF)
        write_64_e_o_c_d(io, cdir_offset, cdir_size)
        write_64_eocd_locator(io, eocd_offset)
      end
      write_e_o_c_d(io, cdir_offset, cdir_size)
    end

    # Reads the End of Central Directory Record (and the Zip64 equivalent if
    # needs be) and returns the number of entries in the archive. This is a
    # convenience method that avoids reading in all of the entry data to get a
    # very quick entry count.
    def count_entries(io)
      read_eocds(io)
      @size
    end

    def ==(other) # :nodoc:
      return false unless other.kind_of?(CentralDirectory)

      @entry_set.entries.sort == other.entries.sort && comment == other.comment
    end

    private

    def write_e_o_c_d(io, offset, cdir_size) # :nodoc:
      tmp = [
        END_OF_CD_SIG,
        0, # @numberOfThisDisk
        0, # @numberOfDiskWithStartOfCDir
        @entry_set ? [@entry_set.size, 0xFFFF].min : 0,
        @entry_set ? [@entry_set.size, 0xFFFF].min : 0,
        [cdir_size, 0xFFFFFFFF].min,
        [offset, 0xFFFFFFFF].min,
        @comment ? @comment.bytesize : 0
      ]
      io << tmp.pack('VvvvvVVv')
      io << @comment
    end

    def write_64_e_o_c_d(io, offset, cdir_size) # :nodoc:
      tmp = [
        ZIP64_END_OF_CD_SIG,
        44, # size of zip64 end of central directory record (excludes signature and field itself)
        VERSION_MADE_BY,
        VERSION_NEEDED_TO_EXTRACT_ZIP64,
        0, # @numberOfThisDisk
        0, # @numberOfDiskWithStartOfCDir
        @entry_set ? @entry_set.size : 0, # number of entries on this disk
        @entry_set ? @entry_set.size : 0, # number of entries total
        cdir_size, # size of central directory
        offset # offset of start of central directory in its disk
      ]
      io << tmp.pack('VQ<vvVVQ<Q<Q<Q<')
    end

    def write_64_eocd_locator(io, zip64_eocd_offset)
      tmp = [
        ZIP64_EOCD_LOCATOR_SIG,
        0, # number of disk containing the start of zip64 eocd record
        zip64_eocd_offset, # offset of the start of zip64 eocd record in its disk
        1 # total number of disks
      ]
      io << tmp.pack('VVQ<V')
    end

    def unpack_64_e_o_c_d(buffer) # :nodoc:
      _, # ZIP64_END_OF_CD_SIG. We know we have this at this point.
      @size_of_zip64_e_o_c_d,
      @version_made_by,
      @version_needed_for_extract,
      @number_of_this_disk,
      @number_of_disk_with_start_of_cdir,
      @total_number_of_entries_in_cdir_on_this_disk,
      @size,
      @size_in_bytes,
      @cdir_offset = buffer.unpack('VQ<vvVVQ<Q<Q<Q<')

      zip64_extensible_data_size =
        @size_of_zip64_e_o_c_d - ZIP64_STATIC_EOCD_SIZE + 12

                                 ''
                               else

    end

      _, # ZIP64_EOCD_LOCATOR_SIG. We know we have this at this point.

**Evaluating ZipKit and security risks**

I'm considering the implications of using ZipKit for importing and testing. The current ZipKit file reader might not be safe for user-supplied archives, given warnings about security risks. While ZipKit allows for path and CRC validations, there's a concern about potential infinite loops. It seems that transitioning to RubyZip Reader could be a viable option, even if it doesn't have CRC validation. We should prioritize security and perhaps avoid using potentially insecure parsers.**Analyzing archive options with Rubyzip and ZipKit**

I'm considering using Rubyzip for metadata parsing, but the archive writer currently employs ZipKit, which uses data descriptors. It's important to verify that ZipKit's writer is compatible with Rubyzip. I found that Zip::InputStream fails, while Zip::File successfully reads the central directory and works with ZipKit. I should test with Zip::File.open_buffer for our StreamWriter using `StringIO` data to see how this all works together. This could lead to a solid solution.

steps.message: One additional security check surfaced in the ZIP library’s own documentation: its reader warns that it has not been security-verified for user-supplied ZIPs. I’m replacing that parser with the already-installed RubyZip central-directory reader, while keeping our own streaming CRC/size checks and ranged S3 IO, so the 500+ GB behavior stays intact without relying on the warned-about parser.

class Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveIO
  READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 8.megabytes

  def initialize(blob)
    @blob = blob
    @position = 0
    @buffer = +"".b
    @buffer_start = 0
    @closed = false
  end

  def size
    @blob.byte_size
  end

  def tell
    @position
  end

  def eof?
    @position >= size
  end

  def seek(offset, whence = IO::SEEK_SET)
    @position = case whence
    when IO::SEEK_SET then offset
    when IO::SEEK_CUR then @position + offset
    when IO::SEEK_END then size + offset
    else raise ArgumentError, "Invalid seek mode"
    end

    raise Errno::EINVAL, "Invalid seek offset" if @position.negative?

    0
  end

  def read(length = nil, output = nil)
    raise IOError, "closed stream" if @closed
    raise ArgumentError, "Negative length #{length}" if length&.negative?

    length ||= size - @position
    return output ? output.clear : "".b if length.zero?
    return output ? nil : nil if eof?

    length = [ length, size - @position ].min
    data = +"".b

    while data.bytesize < length
      fill_buffer unless buffered_position?
      offset = @position - @buffer_start
      bytes_to_copy = [ length - data.bytesize, @buffer.bytesize - offset ].min
      data << @buffer.byteslice(offset, bytes_to_copy)
      @position += bytes_to_copy
    end

    if output
      output.replace(data)
    else
      data
    end
  end

  def close
    @closed = true
  end

  private
    def buffered_position?
      @position >= @buffer_start && @position < @buffer_start + @buffer.bytesize
    end

    def fill_buffer
      @buffer_start = @position
      bytes_to_read = [ READ_BUFFER_SIZE, size - @position ].min
      @buffer = @blob.download_chunk(@position...(@position + bytes_to_read))
    end
end

class Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveEntryIO
  READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 128.kilobytes

  def initialize(entry:)
    @entry = entry
    rewind
  end

  def size
    entry.size
  end

  def rewind
    @stream&.close
    @stream = entry.get_input_stream
    @bytes_read = 0
    @crc = 0
    @verified = false
    0
  end

  def read(length = nil, output = nil)
    if length.nil?
      data = +"".b
      while chunk = read(READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
        data << chunk
      end
    elsif length.negative?
      raise ArgumentError, "Negative length #{length}"
    elsif length.zero?
      data = +"".b
    else
      data = @stream.read(length)
      if data.nil?
        verify_entry
      else
        append(data)
        verify_entry if @stream.eof?
      end
    end

    if output && data
      output.replace(data)
    else
      data
    end
  end

  private
    attr_reader :entry

    def append(chunk)
      @bytes_read += chunk.bytesize
      if @bytes_read > entry.size
        raise Account::DataTransfer::Importer::InvalidArchive, "A ZIP entry is larger than its declared size"
      end

      @crc = Zlib.crc32(chunk, @crc)
    end

    def verify_entry
      return if @verified

      unless @bytes_read == entry.size && @crc == entry.crc
        raise Account::DataTransfer::Importer::InvalidArchive, "A ZIP entry is incomplete or corrupted"
      end

      @verified = true
    end
end

class Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveEntryIO
  READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 128.kilobytes

  def initialize(entry:)
    @entry = entry
    rewind
  end

  def size
    entry.size
  end

  def rewind
    close
    @stream = entry.get_input_stream
    @bytes_read = 0
    @crc = 0
    @verified = false
    @finished = false
    0
  end

  def read(length = nil, output = nil)
    if length.nil?
      data = +"".b
      while chunk = read(READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
        data << chunk
      end
    elsif length.negative?
      raise ArgumentError, "Negative length #{length}"
    elsif length.zero?
      data = +"".b
    elsif @finished
      data = nil
    else
      data = stream.read(length)
      if data.nil? || data.empty?
        verify_entry
        @finished = true
        close
        data = nil
      else
        append(data)
        if stream.eof?
          verify_entry
          @finished = true
          close
        end
      end
    end

    if output && data
      output.replace(data)
    else
      data
    end
  end

  def close
    stream&.close
    @stream = nil
  end

  private
    attr_reader :entry, :stream

    def append(chunk)
      @bytes_read += chunk.bytesize
      if @bytes_read > entry.size
        raise Account::DataTransfer::Importer::InvalidArchive, "A ZIP entry is larger than its declared size"
      end

      @crc = Zlib.crc32(chunk, @crc)
    end

    def verify_entry
      return if @verified

      unless @bytes_read == entry.size && @crc == entry.crc
        raise Account::DataTransfer::Importer::InvalidArchive, "A ZIP entry is incomplete or corrupted"
      end

      @verified = true
    end
end

require "test_helper"
require "zip"

class Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveIOTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "reads a ZIP through ranged storage reads without loading the entire archive" do
    archive = StringIO.new("".b)
    writer = ZipFile::Writer.new(archive)
    writer.add_file("data/cards.jsonl", "{\"id\":\"card-1\"}\n")
    writer.close

    blob = RangeBlob.new(archive.string)
    zip_io = Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveIO.new(blob)
    zip = Zip::File.open_buffer(zip_io)
    entry = zip.get_entry("data/cards.jsonl")
    entry_io = Account::DataTransfer::ArchiveEntryIO.new(entry: entry)

    assert_equal "{\"id\":\"card-1\"}\n", entry_io.read(1024)
    assert_nil entry_io.read(1024)
    assert_operator blob.range_reads, :<, 10
  ensure
    entry_io&.close
  end

  class RangeBlob
    attr_reader :range_reads

    def initialize(data)
      @data = data
      @range_reads = 0
    end

    def byte_size
      @data.bytesize
    end

    def download_chunk(range)
      @range_reads += 1
      @data.byteslice(range.begin, range.size)
    end
  end
end
EOF
